title: pm: the Notify: security doorbell for a private-repository security card carries a bare #N that names no repository
body:
domain:skills#3 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAj7CvjkGXvgXzd6RZ7

Filing gate: should-fix S2 of the contract review of PR #31102 (comment 6704473385, card #30114), outside that card's claim. ⛔ Not a claim. Triage sets the grade and the lane.
class: c · reach: the security seat reading its mailbox, and every seat that rings it for a private-repository card.

## What is owed

On `main` `7faa2375`, `scripts/pm/record-recognisers.mjs` L1307 (`notify:security`) reads `Notify: security · #n` only as triage's labelled PUBLIC card, a bare number with no repository. PR #31102 (card #30114) teaches a private-repository branch: a security finding on a private repository becomes an ordinary `security` issue on that repository, and the holder rings `security#1` with `Notify: security · #N`. That number names no repository, so the security seat cannot tell a private cloud card from a mis-disclosed public card except by who sent it, and cannot open the card without guessing the repository.

Owed: a repository-qualified reading for the private-card doorbell (for example `Notify: security · OWNER/REPO#N`), its `when`/`template` text, the matching line in `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/project-forms.md` (L48) and `security-findings.md`, and self-test cases beside the existing ones (≈L2847–2867). The bare `#n` keeps meaning the public card.

**Level:** `skip-changeset` (nothing published).

Related: #30114, PR #31102.
